How we run the app:

- `GET /up` responds with `200` when the app is ready.
- The app keeps all its data under `storage/`. It must not call external services.

Our QA auto-tests drive the app in a browser and rely on the labels in quotes in each task. Keep them exactly as written, as visible text, a <label>, a placeholder, or an aria-label.

The QA auto-tests also expect:

- Each item of a list (a quiz, a question) sits in its own list item or table row, with its buttons and links inside it.
- Switches are checkboxes (a styled switch is fine if a real checkbox sits under it).
- Confirmations use the browser's native `confirm()` dialog.

Talks have tight schedules, so moderators asked for a timer.

The quiz settings get the time per question: the "Timer minutes" and "Timer seconds" fields (numbers, 0 by default). 0 minutes and 0 seconds means no timer.

With a timer:

- The moderator's big screen shows a countdown in the M:SS format (for example, "1:30" or "0:05") while a question is open. Players don't see the timer.
- The countdown starts when the question opens. Reloading the page doesn't restart it.
- At 0:00, the question finishes by itself, as if the moderator clicked "Finish". The moderator can still click "Finish" earlier.

# Quizzy: design notes

Working notes for Quizzy. Keep them current when the behaviour changes.

## Scope

- Moderator area under `/moderate`, HTTP Basic (`QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME` / `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`).
- Quizzes, single-choice questions with text options, the "Active" switch, move up/down,
  delete, and the preview (a player's walk-through, nothing stored).
- Export and import of a quiz as JSON: "Export" on the quiz page, "Import quiz" on the quiz list.
- The live game: "Start a game" opens a game on the big screen (`/moderate/games/:id`). Phones join
  at `/play/:code` with no account. Everything follows the game live. See "Live game" below.
- After "End quiz": the big screen shows the leaderboard, and the moderator picks the prize winners
  ("Top N", "Draw", "Reset winners"). See "Scoring and prizes" below.
- Not built yet: scores over time and answer statistics of past games (the stylesheet has classes
  for them: `response-*`).

## Running

- `bin/serve` is the only entry point used in production. It needs `SECRET_KEY_BASE` and the two
  moderator variables (it stops with a message if one is missing), runs `bin/rails db:prepare`,
  and starts Puma on `0.0.0.0:$PORT` in the foreground.
- Data: `storage/production.sqlite3` (app), plus `production_cache|queue|cable.sqlite3` from the
  default Solid* setup. Nothing else is written under `storage/`.
- HTTP only: `force_ssl` and `assume_ssl` are off; host authorization is not configured, so any
  host name is accepted. `/up` is Rails' health check (200 when booted).
- Assets: Propshaft serves `app/assets` itself in production (`config.assets.server = true`),
  because there is no proxy in front and no asset precompile step. `quizzy.css` and the font
  come from the design unchanged, apart from the font path. `moderator.css` holds app additions.
- No external calls. Turbo, Stimulus and importmap are vendored by their gems and served locally.
- The QR code is drawn on the server (`rqrcode`, gem installed locally): no QR service is called.
- Live pages poll a fragment every 2-3 seconds. `config/environments/production.rb` keeps those
  requests out of the log (`SilenceRequest` on the `/live` paths), as it does `/up`.

## Routes

| Page | Route | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Quiz list | `GET /moderate` | "New quiz" is a GET button to the form |
| New quiz / save | `GET/POST /moderate/quizzes(/new)` | Saving opens the quiz page |
| Quiz page | `GET /moderate/quizzes/:id` | "Add question" (GET button), "Settings", "Preview" |
| Settings | `GET /moderate/quizzes/:id/edit` | Same form as new; "Delete quiz" with confirm |
| Export | `GET /moderate/quizzes/:id/export` | Quiz as JSON in the only `<pre>`; "Export" link on the quiz page |
| Import form | `GET /moderate/imports/new` | "Import quiz" (GET button) on the quiz list; "Quiz JSON" text area and "Import" button |
| Import | `POST /moderate/imports` | Always a new quiz; redirects to it (303). Errors: 422, nothing saved |
| Preview | `GET /moderate/quizzes/:id/preview` | State lives in the query string (see below) |
| New question | `GET /moderate/quizzes/:quiz_id/questions/new` | Form, four empty rows, Active on |
| Create question | `POST /moderate/quizzes/:quiz_id/questions` | Also handles "Add option" (no save) |
| Edit question | `GET /moderate/questions/:id/edit` | |
| Update / delete | `PATCH/DELETE /moderate/questions/:id` | Delete asks with `confirm()` |
| Move | `PATCH /moderate/questions/:id/move_up` and `/move_down` | Swaps with the neighbour in list order |
| Active switch | `PATCH /moderate/questions/:id/activation` | Form submits on change (Stimulus `auto-submit`) |
| Start a game | `POST /moderate/quizzes/:quiz_id/games` | A new game of the quiz; redirects to its big screen (303) |
| Big screen | `GET /moderate/games/:id` | Layout `screen`. The live region is the whole screen, controls included |
| Big screen state | `GET /moderate/games/:id/live` | Fragment for polls (ETag, 304 when nothing changed) |
| Step | `POST /moderate/games/:id/start`, `/finish`, `/next_question`, `/end_quiz` | Each step is refused (flash, nothing changes) when the phase does not allow it |
| Winners | `POST /moderate/games/:id/top_winners`, `/draw_winners`, `/reset_winners` | Only once the game is finished; refused (flash) before. Buttons: "Top N", "Draw", "Reset winners" |
| Join page | `GET /play/:code` | Name form, then the phone's state. Unknown code: 404. Code is case-insensitive |
| Phone state | `GET /play/:code/live` | Fragment for polls (ETag, 304) |
| Join | `POST /play/:code/join` | Sets the player cookie; a second join from the same browser changes nothing |
| Answer | `POST /play/:code/answers` (`option_id`) | The last pick counts; refused unless the question is open |

## Data

- `quizzes(title, winner_count)`, `questions(quiz_id, text, position, active)`, `options(question_id, text, correct, position)`.
- Positions are unique per quiz and only swapped, never renumbered. A new question gets `max + 1`.
- Deleting a quiz or question deletes its options (dependent destroy). Deleting a quiz also deletes
  its games.
- Games (see "Live game"): `games(quiz_id, code, phase, current_position, revision, finished_at, winner_count)`,
  `game_questions(game_id, position, text, opened_at, closed_at)`, `game_options(game_question_id,
  position, text, correct)`, `players(game_id, name, token, winner)`, `answers(player_id, game_question_id,
  game_option_id, picked_at)` with one answer per player and question (unique index). `picked_at` is the
  time of the player's last pick on that question.

## Option rules (`Question`)

Rows are `{text, correct}` as typed, including empty ones. On save:

1. Rows with blank text are dropped (their checkbox is ignored too).
2. Fewer than two filled rows: "Add at least two options".
3. No correct filled row: "Mark at least one option as correct".
4. An option over 200 characters: "Options can be at most 200 characters long".

Both 2 and 3 are reported together when both fail. Nothing is saved on failure, and the form is
re-rendered with 422 and exactly what was typed. The options are replaced inside the question's
save transaction, so the stored options never change on a failed save. "Active" alone saves
without touching options (`option_rows` is not assigned, so the rules do not run).

## Form details

- Option rows are named `question[options][i][text]` / `[correct]`. Labels: a visually hidden
  "Option N" for the text field (placeholder "Option text"), and a visible "Option N is correct"
  next to the checkbox. Both are real `<label>`s, so QA can find them by label text.
- "Add option" is a submit button with `formnovalidate`, `name=add_option`. The controller adds one
  empty row and re-renders with 200. Nothing is saved.
- Enter in an option field would submit through the first submit button in DOM order. A hidden
  `<button>` with no text comes first in the form, so Enter saves (tested in the system tests).
- The question form has `data-turbo="false"`: it re-renders with plain HTML responses.
- Edit shows the stored options plus empty rows, padded to four rows, like a new question.

Open `http://localhost:3000/moderate` and log in with the moderator credentials.

- Quizzes: create them, add questions (options, the correct ones, "Active"), preview them.

- Games: "Start a game" on a quiz page opens a game on the big screen. The lobby shows the join

- Prizes: after "End quiz" the big screen shows the leaderboard (points, then speed) and each phone

  network, open `/moderate` at an address the phones can reach (for example `http://<laptop-ip>:3000`),

Everything under `/moderate` returns `401` without valid Basic credentials. The phone pages under
`/play/<code>` are public: the code is the game's join link.

```sh
bin/rails test          # models and integration tests
bin/rails test:system   # browser tests on the local Chromium (Cuprite, no chromedriver)
bin/rubocop
```

  the real talk do not share anything.
- Join codes: 5 characters from `Game::CODE_ALPHABET` (no 0, O, 1, I, L), unique.

### Phases

| Phase | Meaning | Moderator's button | Phones |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `lobby` | Players join, nothing is open | "Start" (or "End quiz" when no question is active) | "Hi, <name>!" and waiting |
| `open` | The current question takes answers | "Finish" | Options as buttons, "Your answer" on the pick |
| `closed` | The question is closed, results shown | "Next", or "End quiz" on the last question | "Correct!", "Wrong!" or "No answer", the right option marked |
| `finished` | Over: no joins, no answers | "Top N", "Draw", "Reset winners", "Back to quiz" | "The quiz is over", the place, the points, "You won!" for a winner |

  changes nothing (no revision bump, no broadcast). The screen then shows a flash with the reason.

- Lobby: "Players: N" counts every player who joined this game.

  stream and no ETag ever reveals a correct answer early.

# One run of a quiz. The game keeps its own copy of the quiz's active questions and their options
# (see `create_from_quiz!`), so editing or deactivating questions never changes a game that is
# running or was played.
#
# Phases:
#   lobby    players join, nothing is open yet
#   open     the current question takes answers
#   closed   the current question is closed and its results are shown
#   finished the game is over: no more joins, no more answers; the leaderboard and winners follow
#
# Every phase change and every change of winners bumps `revision`, and tells the screens and phones
# to reload (see `announce`).
class Game < ApplicationRecord
  PHASES = %w[ lobby open closed finished ].freeze
  # Join codes avoid look-alike characters (no 0, O, 1, I, L), so they can be read out loud.
  CODE_ALPHABET = %w[ 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 9 A B C D E F G H J K M N P Q R S T U V W X Y Z ].freeze
  CODE_LENGTH = 5

  belongs_to :quiz
  has_many :game_questions, -> { order(:position) }, dependent: :destroy, inverse_of: :game
  has_many :players, -> { order(:id) }, dependent: :destroy, inverse_of: :game

  before_validation :assign_code, on: :create

  validates :code, presence: true, uniqueness: true, length: { is: CODE_LENGTH }
  validates :phase, inclusion: { in: PHASES }
  validates :revision, numericality: { only_integer: true, greater_than_or_equal_to: 0 }
  validates :winner_count, numericality: { only_integer: true, greater_than_or_equal_to: 1 }

  scope :newest_first, -> { order(created_at: :desc, id: :desc) }

  # Copies the quiz's active questions, in quiz order, with their options, and the quiz's number of
  # winners. Inactive questions are left out, so a game skips them.
  def self.create_from_quiz!(quiz)
    transaction do
      game = create!(quiz: quiz, winner_count: quiz.winner_count)
      quiz.active_questions.each.with_index(1) do |question, position|
        game_question = game.game_questions.create!(text: question.text, position: position)
        question.options.each.with_index(1) do |option, option_position|
          game_question.game_options.create!(text: option.text, correct: option.correct?, position: option_position)
        end
      end
      game
    end
  end

  def lobby? = phase == "lobby"
  def open? = phase == "open"
  def closed? = phase == "closed"
  def finished? = phase == "finished"

  def question_count
    game_questions.count
  end

  def current_question
    return if current_position.nil?

    game_questions.find_by(position: current_position)
  end

  # Questions that were closed, in order: the ones a player's score is counted over.
  def played_question_count
    game_questions.where.not(closed_at: nil).count
  end

  # Moderator transitions. Each returns true when it changed the game, false when the phase did
  # not allow it (for example, a second click on "Next").
  def start!
    transition do
      next false unless lobby? && game_questions.exists?

      open_question_at!(1)
    end
  end

  def finish_question!
    transition do
      next false unless open?

      close_current_question!
      update!(phase: "closed")
    end
  end

  def next_question!
    transition do
      next false unless closed? && current_position < question_count

      open_question_at!(current_position + 1)
    end
  end

  # Ends the game from any phase before "finished". A question that is still open is closed too.
  def end_quiz!
    transition do
      next false if finished?

      close_current_question! if open?
      update!(phase: "finished", finished_at: Time.current)
    end
  end

  # The standings: every player, best first (see Leaderboard). Read fresh each time: not cached.
  def leaderboard
    Leaderboard.new(self)
  end

  def winners
    players.where(winner: true)
  end

  # Winners are picked once the quiz is over. Each returns true when it picked the winners (a draw
  # always picks again, so every click counts), false when the game refuses it.
  def pick_top_winners!
    pick_winners { |board| board.top(winner_count) }
  end

  def draw_winners!(random: Random.new)
    pick_winners { |board| board.draw(winner_count, random: random) }
  end

  # Removes every winner. False when there are none, or the quiz is not over.
  def reset_winners!
    transition do
      next false unless finished? && winners.exists?

      mark_winners([])
      true
    end
  end

  # A player joins. Returns the player, or nil when the game is over. A bad name comes back as an
  # unsaved player with errors.
  def join(name)
    return nil if finished?

    player = Player.new(game: self, name: name)
    announce(:screen) if player.save
    player
  end

  # Records the player's pick for the current question. The last pick counts.
  # Returns :recorded, or the reason it was refused.
  #
  # The phase is checked and the pick saved under the game's lock, so a pick cannot be saved after
  # the moderator has closed the question (the lock is the same one `transition` takes).
  def record_answer(player, option_id)
    return :not_joined unless player&.game_id == id

    result = with_lock do
      question = current_question
      next :closed unless open? && question

      option = question.game_options.find_by(id: option_id)
      next :unknown_option if option.nil?

      save_answer(player, question, option)
      :recorded
    end
    announce(:screen) if result == :recorded
    result
  end

  # What the moderator's screen shows. A change in any of these reloads it.
  def screen_fingerprint
    [ revision, phase, players.count, answered_count ]
  end

  # What a player's page shows.
  def player_fingerprint(player)
    answer = player && current_question && player.answers.find_by(game_question: current_question)
    [ revision, phase, player&.id, answer&.game_option_id, answer&.updated_at&.to_f ]
  end

  def answered_count
    question = current_question
    question ? question.answers.count : 0
  end

  private

  # The live pages subscribe to two streams. Pokes carry no data: the pages fetch their own
  # state, so no page ever gets another player's answer or the correct answers early.
  def announce(channel)
    Turbo::StreamsChannel.broadcast_action_to(self, channel, action: :quizzy_refresh, render: false)
  rescue StandardError => error
    # The change is saved already. The pages poll as well, so a lost poke only delays the update.
    Rails.logger.warn("Live poke for game #{code} failed: #{error.class}: #{error.message}")
  end

  def assign_code
    self.code ||= loop do
      candidate = Array.new(CODE_LENGTH) { CODE_ALPHABET[SecureRandom.random_number(CODE_ALPHABET.size)] }.join
      break candidate unless Game.exists?(code: candidate)
    end
  end

  # Runs the block under a row lock, bumps the revision when it returns truthy, and reloads the
  # screens after the commit.
  def transition
    changed = with_lock do
      result = yield
      if result
        self.revision += 1
        save!
      end
      result
    end
    if changed
      announce(:screen)
      announce(:players)
    end
    changed
  end

  # Picks the winners the block returns (from the leaderboard), once the quiz is over.
  def pick_winners
    transition do
      next false unless finished?

      mark_winners(yield(leaderboard))
      true
    end
  end

  # Only these players are winners from now on. Runs inside `transition`.
  def mark_winners(chosen)
    Player.where(game_id: id).update_all(winner: false)
    Player.where(id: chosen.map(&:id)).update_all(winner: true) if chosen.any?
  end

  def open_question_at!(position)
    game_questions.find_by!(position: position).update!(opened_at: Time.current, closed_at: nil)
    update!(phase: "open", current_position: position)
  end

  def close_current_question!
    current_question&.update!(closed_at: Time.current)
  end

  def save_answer(player, question, option)
    answer = Answer.find_or_initialize_by(player: player, game_question: question)
    answer.update!(game_option: option, picked_at: Time.current)
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique
    # Two requests from the same player raced to create the answer. The second one updates it.
    retry
  end
end

# A live page keeps one region up to date by polling a fragment of itself. Each fragment carries an
# ETag over the state it shows, so a poll that finds nothing new gets a 304 and no HTML.
module LiveRegion
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  # ETag is built from the state after that.

    if request.headers["If-None-Match"].to_s.split(",").map(&:strip).include?(etag)

    else
      render :live, layout: false
    end
  end
end
